stories.title: Bullish consensus on DELL
stories.sub: The feed is bullish because Dell's fiscal Q3 2027 results, reported around Nov 24-25, 2026, were a large beat.
stories.line: 5 bullish vs 0 bearish posts. Is the move already priced in?

cards.title: Bottom line
cards.text: The feed is bullish because Dell's fiscal Q3 2027 results, reported around Nov 24-25, 2026, were a large beat. Revenue roughly doubled to a record $54.9B and adjusted EPS was $9.45 against $6.61 expected. Dell booked $60.2B of AI server orders, its AI backlog reached $132B, it raised FY27 revenue guidance to about $202B and it added a $25B buyback. How much was already priced in is disputed. Some reports say shares fell about 7% as analysts cut price targets on margin and inventory worries, and others list Dell among the big premarket movers, so the stock's reaction is not a clean confirmation of the bullish view.

items.text: record revenue of $54.9B (+103% y/y). AI-optimized server revenue was $22.0B (+291% y/y), and adjusted EPS was $9.45 vs about $6.61 consensus. Reported diluted EPS is lower, about $8.82.

AI orders were $60.2B in the quarter and the AI backlog is a record $132.3B. FY27 revenue guidance rose to about $202B vs about $194B consensus, the third raise this year. Q4 revenue guidance is reportedly about $56.3B.
The board added $25B to the Class C share buyback. Dell returned a record $4.9B to shareholders in Q3 through buybacks and dividends.

The market reaction is mixed. Benzinga reports shares falling about 7% as analysts cut targets; for example, Wells Fargo stayed at Overweight but lowered its target from $545 to $400. An Investing.com analysis describes a 19% selloff tied to margin risk. Expectations were very high going in: shares had already run up on Nvidia's results, and the options market implied about a 10% move.

The bear case centres on quality of growth. AI servers carry thinner margins than traditional infrastructure, and inventory rose to about $29.4B, which ties up working capital even as Dell expands buybacks.
Price action after the report, and whether the gap holds through the holiday-shortened week of Nov 25-27, 2026
Gross-margin trend and inventory or working-capital levels in Q4 FY27. Results are expected around late Feb 2027.
Conversion of the $132B AI backlog into shipments, and new orders from neocloud and sovereign customers
Memory and component cost inflation, and supply of Nvidia GPUs and next-generation racks
AI server revenue at low margins could limit EPS upside even as revenue doubles

items.lead: AI capex cyclicality and customer concentration
items.text: order cancellations, delays or financing stress at large AI customers could hit the backlog
Rising inventory and component costs, which could pressure cash flow and guidance credibility

stories.title: Bullish consensus on SPCX
stories.sub: The bullish tone on SpaceX (SPCX) comes mainly from analyst actions.
stories.line: 3 bullish vs 0 bearish posts. Is the move already priced in?

cards.title: Bottom line
cards.text: The bullish tone on SpaceX (SPCX) comes mainly from analyst actions. Mizuho named SpaceX a top idea at Outperform with a $205 target, Jefferies started at Buy with a $210 target, and ARK published bullish work on orbital compute and launch-cost leadership. The stock itself is weak, though: reports put it at about $126-133, below its $135 June IPO price, and it slipped premarket despite the new ratings. That gap suggests the bullish story is not fully priced in, but it also shows the market discounting risks such as lockup supply and customer concentration.

items.text: TipRanks and Blockonomi describe it as a coverage transfer that kept the Outperform rating and $205 target. It calls SpaceX the 'ultimate vertical integration play' across launch, Starlink and AI infrastructure, and says reusable rockets cut launch costs about 85-90%.
Jefferies initiated at Buy with a $210 target, Bank of America has a Buy at $275 and Evercore an Outperform at $275. Roughly 28 of 35 analysts rate the stock Buy.
SpaceX's orbital compute could reach cost parity with terrestrial data centres by about 2028. ARK also says SpaceX's chip demand could squeeze suppliers' margins. Both are long-dated and speculative.

The stock slipped premarket despite the upgrades. Reports tie the weakness to Anthropic, cited as SpaceX's biggest customer, trading below its own IPO price, and to J.P. Morgan commentary linking a possible Tesla merger to S&P 500 entry.
SpaceX's first public results showed revenue up 92% y/y to $7.8B and adjusted EBITDA up 191% to $3.5B, driven by Starlink and AI-related demand.
Further lockup expiries and insider or early-holder supply. Earlier unlocks in Aug 2026 released more than 328M shares.
The next quarterly report, with Starlink subscriber and revenue growth and AI/compute segment disclosures
Starship flight cadence and reuse milestones, which underpin the cost-reduction thesis
Any developments on a Tesla combination, S&P 500 eligibility, and the health of AI customers such as Anthropic
much of the bull case, such as orbital compute and AI infrastructure, is years out and hard to verify
a pullback by a major customer like Anthropic could hit growth expectations
Supply overhang from lockup expiries, plus key-person and governance risk tied to Elon Musk and possible related-party deals with Tesla or xAI

stories.title: Bullish consensus on META
stories.sub: The feed's optimism centres on Muse, Meta's personal AI agent launched in the US in September 2026.
stories.line: 2 bullish vs 0 bearish posts. Is the move already priced in?

cards.title: Bottom line
cards.text: The feed's optimism centres on Muse, Meta's personal AI agent launched in the US in September 2026. Fortune reported on Nov 25 that Amazon and Meta are in talks to restore Muse's shopping access to Amazon after Amazon blocked it. Muse is also expanding to the UK, and Meta is using Instagram to turn agent activity into ad gains. META rose on these reports, but the stock had been under pressure after Q3 because of heavy capex: 2026 capex of $135-145B and the first negative free cash flow since 2012. So the Muse optimism is partly a rebound from a de-rated base rather than a fully priced-in story.

items.text: Fortune, relayed by TechCrunch, reported several rounds of talks to let Muse shop on Amazon again. The talks are described as fluid, no deal is guaranteed, a deal reportedly needs approval from both CEOs, and the main sticking point is Amazon's advertising business.
Amazon had blocked Muse as an unauthorised agent that did not identify itself, and Meta had refused to drop Amazon from Muse. The dispute is a test of how open-web agentic shopping will work.

Muse is rolling out to UK users, which extends its reach beyond the US. CNBC reports that Meta is using Instagram to turn Muse activity into an ad boost, while saying Muse conversations do not directly feed ad targeting.

Q4 revenue guidance of $73-76B was above consensus. However, 2026 capex was raised to $135-145B and Q3 capex was $34.9B, producing negative FCF of about $2.1B, and the stock fell about 7% after the report.
Whether Amazon and Meta reach a Muse access deal, and on what ad or revenue-share terms. Timing is not yet known.
Muse adoption and engagement data, plus the progress of its UK and further international rollouts
Q4 2026 earnings and 2027 capex guidance, likely in late Jan 2027
Holiday-season ad pricing and impressions, and any Instagram agentic-shopping launch
The AI capex burden may keep FCF weak and pressure the valuation if Muse monetisation lags
The Amazon talks rest on a single uncorroborated report and could fail. Other retailers may also block agents.
Regulatory, privacy and consumer-trust risk around agents acting on users' behalf, especially in the UK and EU

stories.title: BTC under pressure
stories.sub: BTC slipped below $59K in Asian trading on Nov 25.
stories.line: 5 bearish vs 0 bullish posts. Continuation or washout?

cards.title: Bottom line
cards.text: BTC slipped below $59K in Asian trading on Nov 25. The negative mood comes from steady spot-ETF outflows, miner stress (hashrate down about 8% YoY, the first annual decline since 2021, with hashprice near record lows) and sentiment pinned at Extreme Fear (Fear & Greed index 10-13). Extreme-fear readings and miner capitulation have often come near washout lows in past cycles, but the flow data does not yet show a reversal: ETF outflow streaks keep resuming after brief one-day inflows.

items.text: BTC traded about $59.3K-$60.7K on Nov 24, failed to retake Monday's high, then broke below $59K on Nov 25. It was near $62-64K a week earlier.

US spot BTC ETFs lost $1.91B over seven straight sessions (Nov 5-13). After a brief inflow they lost $306M on Nov 18, taking assets to a 3-month low of about $77.7B. IBTimes put November net outflows near $2.9B mid-month. The feed's figure of about $5B for the month was not independently confirmed.

Glassnode puts hashrate near 933 EH/s, about 8% lower YoY. Luxor hashprice is around $28-29/PH/day, a record low. Miners are reportedly selling BTC to repay loans and fund AI and data-center pivots, which adds supply.
the Crypto Fear & Greed index read 10 on Nov 19 and about 13 on Nov 25. That deep pessimism is a contrarian washout signal, but it has persisted for weeks without a durable bounce.

items.lead: Feed items not verified in search
items.text: the Coldcard seed flaw/theft (1,778 BTC) and the Moscow Exchange launching BTC/ETH/USDT trading on Dec 1.
Daily US spot BTC/ETH ETF flows. A multi-day run of net inflows would be the first sign that the outflow trend is reversing.
Difficulty adjustment around Nov 27, projected at about +8.5%. That would squeeze miner margins further and could force more selling or capitulation.
FOMC decision on Dec 9. Markets price roughly a 92-97% chance of a 25bp hike. A hawkish surprise or follow-through would tighten liquidity for risk assets.
$59K-$60K (the area that just broke) and $62-64K (last week's range) as resistance. A move back above $60.7K would negate the Nov 24-25 breakdown.
miner capitulation and extreme fear have historically come near local bottoms, so a sharp short-covering rally is possible once ETF outflows dry up.
a Fed hiking cycle and a firm dollar could keep ETF redemptions and miner selling going, with no catalyst yet to absorb that supply.
Security incidents (such as the reported Coldcard flaw) or exchange stress could add forced selling and hurt confidence.

stories.title: CL under pressure
stories.sub: Crude is near three-month lows: WTI around $80-81.5 and Brent around $89-91 as of Nov 24-25, after a third straight weekly loss.
stories.line: 4 bearish vs 0 bullish posts. Continuation or washout?

cards.title: Bottom line
cards.text: Crude is near three-month lows: WTI around $80-81.5 and Brent around $89-91 as of Nov 24-25, after a third straight weekly loss. The selling is driven by supply: supplies are recovering, Libya's pipeline has reopened, Saudi Yanbu refining is back to full capacity and a surplus is expected. Geopolitical headlines (Houthi strikes on Saudi targets, Iran/US escalation talk, Ukraine strikes on Russian refineries) are limiting the downside but have not reversed the trend.

items.text: WTI fell $3.24 (-3.9%) and Brent fell $3.20 (-3.5%) on Monday Nov 23, settling near 3-month lows. WTI then slipped below $80 intraday. The prior Friday's settles were WTI $83.98 and Brent $92.57, down 5.2% and 3.4% for the week.
recovering global supply, the reopened Libyan pipeline, Saudi Aramco's Yanbu refinery back at full rates by Nov 19, and expectations of a growing surplus.
Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites lifted Brent 3.3% on Nov 12, but those spikes have faded fast. The market is treating repeated headlines as event risk, not a lasting supply loss.

the US blockade and conflict cycle (war from Feb 28, an MoU on Jun 17, the blockade reimposed in July, warnings in August) pushed WTI above $105 in April. Current prices are far below that, so a renewed escalation such as strikes on Iranian leaders would be a big upside shock from a low base.
The Brent-WTI spread widened to about $9.1 from $7.3, which suggests the risk is concentrated in the Middle East/Atlantic basin rather than in US supply.
OPEC+ meeting on Nov 29 setting 2027 quotas, with about 2M b/d of cuts still in place. Extending or deepening cuts could put a floor under prices; easing them would add to surplus fears.
reported debate over strikes on Iranian leadership, Iran's vow to break the blockade, and tanker cyberattack probes. Any hit to Hormuz flows is the main upside risk.
Russia's retaliation for Ukrainian refinery strikes (Russian refinery activity was reportedly down sharply) and any moves against export infrastructure.
WTI $80 (round number and 3-month low) and Brent $89. Reclaiming WTI $84 and Brent $92.5, last Friday's closes, would negate the latest leg down.
Gulf escalation (Iran or the Houthis hitting Saudi or Hormuz flows) could quickly add $10+ of risk premium, as in April-July 2026.
if OPEC+ unwinds cuts and demand softens under Fed tightening, the surplus could push prices well below $80.
Headlines drive the market and are volatile, with large one-day swings in both directions (±3-4%).

stories.title: GC under pressure
stories.sub: Gold broke below $3,500 for the first time since Sept 2025, down about a third from its Jan 28 record near $5,589.
stories.line: 4 bearish vs 0 bullish posts. Continuation or washout?

cards.title: Bottom line
cards.text: Gold broke below $3,500 for the first time since Sept 2025, down about a third from its Jan 28 record near $5,589. The main driver is a Fed now expected to hike in December after hot inflation (October core PCE at 3.3% YoY vs 3.2% expected, GDP growth 4.3%), along with a firm dollar. Gold fell even as yields slipped, which suggests liquidation and positioning pressure. Analysts see $3,400-$3,500 as major weekly support, and a hold there could set up a washout; a sustained break would open further downside.

items.text: gold hit a 14-month low near $3,880 on Nov 12 and broke below $3,885-$3,900 support by Nov 19. It then fell 2% to about $3,482 on Nov 25, with some reports showing lows near $3,426. One report has a bounce to about $3,575 early Nov 26; levels should be checked against live data.
CME FedWatch implied about 92-97% odds of a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC. Hawkish Fed commentary and Goldman's note that markets price about four hikes raise the opportunity cost of holding gold.
October core PCE at 3.3% YoY beat expectations. Inflation pressure tied to oil and Middle East supply fears has, unusually, hurt gold by pushing up Fed hike odds rather than lifting gold as a hedge.
Gold fell despite lower 10-year yields and a softer dollar on Nov 25. This is the 'strange' behavior cited in the feed, consistent with forced liquidation or de-risking rather than a pure rates move.
Silver is falling faster (-3% vs -1% for gold), which suggests broad selling across precious metals. Longer-term bulls still point to central-bank buying.
FOMC decision on Dec 9 (meeting Dec 8-9). The hike is largely priced in, so a less hawkish tone or a 'one and done' message could spark short covering; signals of more hikes would add pressure.
November CPI on Dec 10, the day after the FOMC, as a check on the inflation trend.
$3,400-$3,500 major support. A weekly close below $3,400 would mark a sustained breakdown; reclaiming $3,885-$3,900 would signal a reversal.
Dollar index and real yields, plus central-bank purchase data, as signs of whether dip-buying is emerging.
a dovish Fed surprise, an escalation shock (Iran, Gulf) or renewed central-bank buying could trigger a sharp rebound from $3,400-$3,500 support.
if inflation stays sticky and the Fed signals a longer hiking cycle, gold could break $3,400 and extend toward lower supports.
Exact price levels differ across sources and liquidity is thin around the US Thanksgiving holiday, which can exaggerate moves.

stories.sub: The swing from +2 to -57 lines up with a renewed AI-credit selloff on Nov 25: Nvidia gave back part of its ~30% Huang-reinstatement rally, and CoreWeave debt traded at distressed levels (bond yields o

cards.title: Bottom line
cards.text: The swing from +2 to -57 lines up with a renewed AI-credit selloff on Nov 25: Nvidia gave back part of its ~30% Huang-reinstatement rally, and CoreWeave debt traded at distressed levels (bond yields of 17-18%, CDS at record wides). Index futures fell about 2% (S&P) and 3% (Nasdaq). Thin Thanksgiving-week liquidity, the October PCE release and tariff headlines add macro noise ahead of the Dec 8-9 FOMC.

items.text: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov 23 (8-K; Trump said he was personally involved), and the stock closed more than 30% higher. It fell about 5.9% on Nov 24 and more than 5% again premarket Nov 25, so the 'Huang return' relief rally has faded.

items.lead: CoreWeave is the focus of the stress
items.text: shares fell about 13% premarket and its 2031 notes yielded more than 17-18%. Reports say 5-year CDS posted their biggest jump on record, implying a default probability above 70%. In early November, Deutsche Bank had CDS at about 1,289bp, above the October peak.

Morgan Stanley and MUFG are reportedly preparing to sell a $4.5B GPU-backed loan tied to CoreWeave's Meta contract, with talk of 7-7.5%. That backs the feed's 'banks offloading AI data center loans' theme, and the pricing gap between Meta-backed and unsecured CoreWeave debt is very large.
Reports also cite worry about AI capex returns and debt levels across Oracle, Nebius and Dell, plus reports of possible new US tariffs ahead of the inflation data.

I could not verify the feed's claim of gold below $3,500. The latest reports I found (Nov 19) put gold at a 14-month low near $3,850-3,900, about 34% below its Jan 28 record of $5,589. Analysts flagged $3,500 as the next target if that support breaks.
Oct PCE/core PCE, jobless claims (moved up a day) and consumer confidence, Wed Nov 25. The Cleveland Fed nowcast was ~3.8% y/y headline and ~3.2% core.
US markets are closed Thu Nov 26 for Thanksgiving and close early Fri Nov 27. Thin liquidity can magnify moves.
Launch and pricing of the $4.5B CoreWeave/Meta-backed loan (expected next week), plus CoreWeave CDS and 2031-bond yield levels.
FOMC decision Dec 8-9, 2026, with inflation running well above target.
Nvidia's analyst upgrades (Melius, Bernstein) and strong fundamentals could pull dip-buyers in after the panic, as happened on Nov 23.
Distress could spread from neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius to hyperscaler and Oracle credit, and to the banks holding data-center loans, if loan sales fail or are priced at wide discounts.
A hot PCE print or tariff news could push yields higher. The 10-year has recently been near multi-year highs, which would add to pressure on long-duration tech.

stories.title: Main risks flagged today
stories.sub: The bearish posts center on AI-infrastructure credit risk.
stories.line: 72 important bearish posts. Review them before adding risk.

cards.title: Bottom line
cards.text: The bearish posts center on AI-infrastructure credit risk. CoreWeave's debt prices in distress, banks are trying to move data-center loan exposure, and doubts about the returns on AI capex are hitting chip leaders even after Nvidia's leadership drama ended. The credit signals are serious for highly levered neoclouds. Whether the stress spreads to the wider market is less certain, because secured and investment-grade-backed AI debt is still trading near par.

items.text: CoreWeave 5-year CDS have been above about 1,300bp, and reports say they posted a record one-day jump. Analysts treat anything above 1,000bp as distress, and one report says the spreads imply a default probability above 70%. Its 2031 bonds yield 17-18%.

banks led by Morgan Stanley and MUFG want to sell a $4.5B GPU-backed loan. It is only investment-grade-eligible because of Meta's contract, while CoreWeave itself is junk-rated. Separate reports say banks are pulling back on AI data-center loans in Asia.
CoreWeave's delayed-draw term loans reportedly still trade near par, and the Meta-backed loan talk of 7-7.5% suggests lenders separate contract-backed collateral from CoreWeave's unsecured credit.

Nvidia's pullback after its Huang-return rally, along with drops in Oracle, Nebius and Dell, shows the market questioning AI capex economics and not only CoreWeave. Oracle has already sold off before on bond-market stress.

inflation above target (Sep PCE 3.6% y/y), high Treasury yields, possible tariffs, and gold down about 34% from its January record point to a tighter-Fed and higher-real-rate environment that hurts levered borrowers.
